subject: Re: Redwood demo & next steps — Enterprisecorp buying process + security checklist
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T15:10:00Z
Subject: Redwood demo follow-up and security questionnaire

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team found the latency/cost discussion helpful. Per our call, I'm attaching our initial security questionnaire (PDF) and a procurement checklist so your team can see our buying process. A few key items from our side: 

- Economic buyer: John Park (cc'd on this thread)
- Procurement lead: procurement@enterprisecorp.com (internal)
- Decision criteria: performance under sustained load, SOC2 + KMS integration, and predictable unit cost with committed pricing
- Timeline: target decision in ~6 weeks (pilot -> eval -> procurement/legal)

Can you send over a mutual action plan and a draft SOW? Also, procurement asked whether Redwood can consider onboarding/renewal discounts and whether SLA exceptions are possible for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: Enterprisecorp_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf, Procurement_Checklist_Enterprisecorp.xlsx

Best,
Samantha
Director of Platform Engineering
Enterprisecorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@enterprisecorp.com>, John Park <john.park@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up and security questionnaire

Samantha — great to meet you and thanks for sending the materials. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of call:
- Interested in a pilot for our hosted inference (model A variant) with 50 concurrent connections for 2 weeks to validate latency and cost
- Security team will validate SOC2/KMS details (you sent the questionnaire; we will respond)

2) Immediate next steps (proposed MAP):
- Tue 5/4: Redwood provides completed security questionnaire and draft SOW
- Wed 5/5: Pilot setup + onboarding call
- Week of 5/18: Pilot evaluation and metrics review
- Week of 6/1: Procurement & legal review, finalize contract

3) Procurement asks noted: discounts and SLA exceptions. I've cc'd Aditya (revenue lead) and Vivek (enterprise sales) to flag that we may need an internal approval for any exceptions. Monica in legal will also need to review redlines — copying her on a separate internal note.

I've attached a Mutual Action Plan and a draft SOW for your review. Will complete the security questionnaire and send it back by EOD 5/2.

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Enterprisecorp_v1.xlsx, Draft_SOW_v2.docx

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: John Park <john.park@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: procurement@enterprisecorp.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up and security questionnaire

Marissa — thanks for the quick recap. A couple clarifications from procurement/security: 

- We require an up-to-date SOC2 report and details on your KMS/HSM key management (can be redacted)
- We have a standard procurement checklist attached; legal will want to see indemnity and data-processing terms
- Regarding SLA: our platform teams prefer a 99.9% uptime SLA with defined credits for downtime. Would Redwood entertain that for Enterprise deals?
- On discounts: procurement typically negotiates a one-time onboarding credit or a commit-based discount. Can you confirm any flexibility so we can move internal approvals quickly?

Attachment: Procurement_Checklist_Enterprisecorp.xlsx

John Park
Head of Procurement
Enterprisecorp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T10:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Enterprisecorp buying process — approval needed

Team — forwarding Enterprisecorp's procurement note and checklist. Key asks that require decisions/feedback: 

1) SLA: Enterprisecorp wants 99.9% uptime SLA with credits. It's above our standard hosted SLA; legal will need to confirm acceptable penalties/limits.
2) Discounts: they asked about onboarding credit or commit-based discount. Procurement expects a number to route through their finance cycle.
3) Security: they require SOC2 and KMS integration details (we can provide SOC2 report; KMS pattern is supported but Monica please confirm any contractual language changes).

Attachments forwarded: Procurement_Checklist_Enterprisecorp.xlsx, Enterprisecorp_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf

Can you advise on: (a) discount guardrails (percent thresholds that need executive approval), (b) whether legal approves SLA exception and sample redline language, and (c) whether we should propose a pilot-specific credit vs. annual commit discount? I can draft language for procurement once we have approvals.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Enterprisecorp buying process — approval needed

Marissa — reviewed the checklist and questionnaire. Quick takes: 

- SLA exception: legal is generally comfortable with a 99.9% uptime SLA provided we include a clear cap on liability and exclude scheduled maintenance and force majeure. We should propose service credits (e.g., 5% of monthly fee per major outage up to 50%) rather than liquidated damages. I'll prepare a redline template.
- Security questionnaire: provide the redacted SOC2 and a KMS overview (we can provide architecture diagram and KMS responsibilities).
- Discounts: legal doesn't sign off on discounts but recommends finance approve. For commercial speed, if Aditya/Revenue approves up to 15% off list for a one-year commit we can offer that; anything above 15% should be escalated to Sales Leadership and Finance with ARR justification.

I'll draft the SLA redline and a short email you can send to procurement.

—Monica
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Enterprisecorp buying process — approval needed

Team — I approve a commercial exception: up to 15% discount on one-year committed ARR and pre-approved pilot credit up to $10k. Anything beyond 15% requires Sales Leadership + Finance sign-off; provide estimated ARR and CAC for escalation. SLA exception for 99.9% is approved from a go/no-go perspective pending Monica's redline language in the contract.

Aditya Rao
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@enterprisecorp.com>, John Park <john.park@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T11:05:00Z
Subject: Updated next steps & approvals — Redwood x Enterprisecorp

Samantha/John — quick update following our internal review: 

- Security: we'll send a redacted SOC2 and a KMS overview by EOD 5/4. Monica will provide a contract redline for SLA wording.
- SLA: Redwood can agree to a 99.9% uptime SLA with standard liability cap; Monica will share proposed redline.
- Discounts/credits: Pre-approved: up to 15% discount on a 12-month commit and a pilot onboarding credit up to $10k. If procurement needs a larger commercial concession, we'll need to escalate to Finance for approval.

Next steps:
- Today 5/4: Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS overview + MAP (I'll attach)
- 5/5: Onboarding/pilot setup
- 5/18: Pilot metrics review

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Enterprisecorp_v1.xlsx (updated), SOC2_Redacted_2026.pdf

If this looks good I can circulate a mutual action plan for signatures and coordinate DocuSign once procurement confirms contract contacts.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
